sentences.text: Rolfodon is an extinct genus of shark belonging to the family Chlamydoselachidae, a group closely related to modern frilled sharks.
Although related to living relatives, it can be distinguished from them by differences in tooth shape.
The holotype tooth of the species R. goliath is about 20mm high and features straightened, upright cusps with smooth, unornamented enameloid.
The species R. goliath, found in the Late Campanian of Angola, could grow to very large sizes.

The species R. tatere survived the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction, with fossils extending its known existence by over 10 million years from the Late Cretaceous of Antarctica to the Early Paleocene of New Zealand.
The genus Rolfodon was described by Cappetta, Morrison, and Adnet in 2019.
The earliest known fossil teeth of Rolfodon date to the Late Cretaceous Turonian/Santonian boundary in Japan.
Fossil remains of Rolfodon have been found worldwide, including Japan, Canada, Austria, New Zealand, Angola, Ecuador, and Antarctica.
Most species of Rolfodon were previously classified within the genus Chlamydoselachus.
Research by Cappetta et al. in 2019 determined that the species formerly known as C. fiedleri actually belongs to the genus Rolfodon.
The type species of the genus Rolfodon is Rolfodon ludvigseni.
Rolfodon lived from the Campanian to the Tortonian, spanning from 83.6 to 7.246 million years ago.
